issues.description: The problem description lists attribute names as 'lectureName', 'inscribedStudents', and 'guestStudents' while the UML diagram and the solution implementation use 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents'. This name mismatch (text vs UML/solution) can confuse students about the exact attribute names and the expected constructor parameter order.
issues.suggestedFix: Make attribute naming consistent across the problem text, UML diagram, template, and solution. Either update the problem statement text to use 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents' (matching the UML and solution), or change the UML and solution to use 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents'. Also clarify the constructor parameter order in the problem statement to match the UML.

issues.description: The problem statement's prose (line listing attributes) refers to the attributes as 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents', while the UML diagram and the code (solution) use the more explicit names 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents'. Update the prose in problem_statement.md to list 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents' (to match the UML and code), or alternatively change the UML and code to use 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents' if the shorter names are preferred.
